leaves.name: serviceCallChain
leaves.best_concept: number customer service calls >= 4 and total day minutes <= 220
leaves.why: A gate that opens at four or more customer-service calls for customers who are not heavy daytime users (one call earlier at light use, shut at 300 day minutes), peaks at five calls and falls back for the few customers with six or more.

leaves.name: dayChargeBoost
leaves.best_concept: total day charge > 32 or number customer service calls >= 4
leaves.why: A day-charge hinge from about 32 dollars that also carries the service-call chain's output, so the complaint signal is counted a second time.

leaves.name: serviceCallSpike
leaves.why: A single hinge rising linearly from four service calls, unaffected by day use.

leaves.name: heavyDayUse
leaves.why: A hinge from about 220 day minutes read out twice: the steep upper branch of the model's response to daytime use.

leaves.name: dayMinutesRamp
leaves.why: A negative near-linear ramp above about 130 day minutes, on for the whole training split, that offsets the direct day-charge term for moderate users.

leaves.name: twoStateFlag
leaves.why: A flag for states 45 and 49 (Virginia, West Virginia) with a small negative weight.

overall_function: The network is a sigmoid of a bias plus additive parts. The largest is a linear sum of direct edges whose leading terms are the international plan (raising the score), the voice-mail plan (lowering it, outweighing its positive message-count term), day charge, evening and international usage and a few state codes. Two inputs interact nonlinearly: the customer-service call count and daytime use. A deep chain of hinges detects many service calls among customers who are not heavy daytime users (its threshold rises with day minutes and it shuts off for very heavy users), feeds the output directly and is re-counted inside a day-charge hinge; a separate linear spike on service calls keeps the score rising for the most frequent callers. Daytime use is read three times (direct day-charge edge, day-charge hinge, heavy-use hinge) and once negatively (a near-linear ramp), giving a flat-to-falling response for light and moderate users and a steep rise for heavy users; four small state flags adjust the score slightly, and the remaining state codes, area code 510, evening calls, night minutes and calls and international minutes are unconnected and ignored.
customer_terms: The model predicts a customer is more likely to leave when they hold an international plan, when they have called customer service several times (the gate opens at a few calls for typical daytime use and one call earlier for light users), and when they are heavy daytime users; a voice-mail plan lowers the predicted chance of leaving. The two risk gates are partly exclusive: the service-call gate is suppressed for heavy daytime users, who are already scored high on usage alone, and for customers who make a great many calls the gate eases while a separate linear term keeps the score up. Night, evening and international minutes play at most a small linear role, account length barely matters, and most states make no difference.
stuck: Nothing blocked the work. Three things cost time: the probe and subgroup tools want the dataset's raw column names rather than the renamed node names (one failed batch); a leaf's exit cannot serve as another leaf's entry, so the two serial hand-offs (chain into the day-charge unit, heavy-use unit into the two-state flag) needed identity nodes; and structural coverage counts an exit as covered only when every one of its outgoing edges sits in some annotation, so the two hand-off edges had to be listed in the root and the compositions were undone and recreated once.
